title: Getting Started: First Time at the Machine
cardTitle: I just opened the box… where do I start?

meta.excerpt: Get organized, set up your machine, and knit your very first rows with confidence.
meta.why_use: Perfect if you just unpacked your machine and feel overwhelmed by all the parts. This walkthrough helps you get oriented, choose the right yarn, and knit your first simple fabric.

steps.title: Welcome — let’s get you oriented
body: You just opened the box. There are parts everywhere. Take a breath — you don’t have to figure it out alone.
We’ll walk through what’s in the box, your manual, yarn choice, basic setup, and knitting your very first rows.

steps.title: What’s in the box?
body: Every machine model is a little different, but most include a similar set of parts. Let’s make sure you recognize the basics.
checklist: Needlebed (the long bed with all the needles)
Carriage (the part you slide across the needles)
Sponge bar or needle retaining strip

fields.name: inventory_status
fields.label: How are you feeling about the parts?

options.label: I can identify most of these parts.
I think I’m missing something important.
I’m not sure what I’m looking at yet.

helperText.text: Many used or older machines arrive with a few tools missing. That doesn’t mean you can’t get started. We’ll focus on the essentials and you can replace missing tools over time.

steps.title: Do you have your manual?
body: Your machine’s manual is your best friend. It shows you how your specific model was designed to be threaded, cast on, and used safely.

fields.name: manual_status
fields.label: Do you have your machine’s manual?

options.label: Yes, I have the original manual.
I found a PDF or copy online.
No, I don’t have a manual yet.

helperText.text: When you have a moment, search online for your machine brand and model plus the word "manual". Many manuals are available as free PDFs. For now, we’ll keep things simple and safe.

steps.title: Choose yarn that sets you up for success
body: The wrong yarn can make a great machine feel impossible. For your first time, we want smooth and cooperative.
Avoid dark, fuzzy, very textured, or sticky yarns. A smooth, light-colored yarn that matches your machine’s recommended weight is ideal.

fields.name: yarn_status
fields.label: Do you have suitable yarn for your first practice?

options.label: Yes, I have smooth, light-colored yarn.
I’m not sure if my yarn is a good match.
No, I don’t think I have suitable yarn yet.

helperText.text: As a quick check: if it’s fuzzy, very hairy, bumpy, or very dark, save it for later. Choose something smoother and lighter in color to make it easier to see your stitches.

steps.title: Basic machine setup
body: Before you knit your first rows, let’s make sure your machine is stable and ready.
You don’t need every accessory to be perfect — we’re just aiming for a safe, simple setup.
checklist: The machine is on a sturdy table or stand.
The yarn mast / tension unit is attached and upright.
The carriage can slide smoothly from left to right and back.
The needles move freely in and out of working position.
The row counter (if you have one) is reset to 000.

fields.name: setup_feeling
fields.label: How does your setup feel right now?

options.label: Ready — I think everything is in place.
Almost — I’m unsure about one or two things.

helperText.text: It’s okay to pause here. Double-check that nothing is caught under the carriage, the machine is level, and no tools are resting on the needlebed. Small adjustments can make a big difference.

steps.title: Knit your very first rows
body: This isn’t about making something perfect — it’s about feeling your machine knit.
We’ll cast on simply and knit a small rectangle of fabric so you can see stitches forming and gain confidence.
checklist: Bring a small group of needles to working position in the center of the bed (for example, 20–30 needles).
Use a basic cast-on method recommended in your manual or a simple e-wrap cast-on.
Set your tension dial somewhere in the middle of its range.
Thread the yarn through the tension unit and carriage as your manual shows.
Knit 20–30 rows, watching the needles and stitches as you go.

fields.name: first_rows_status
fields.label: Were you able to knit a small piece of fabric?

options.label: Yes — I knit my first little rectangle!
Not yet — I ran into trouble.

helperText.text: Every knitter fights the first few rows. If stitches are dropping or the carriage feels tight, it doesn’t mean you’re doing it wrong — it just means the machine is new to you. Make a quick note of what’s happening so you can ask for help or come back with fresh eyes.

steps.title: Great job — here’s what’s next
body: If you’ve knit even a handful of rows, you’ve done the hardest part — you started.
From here, you can practice a few basics, or move on to learning how to knit and measure a swatch.
